sentences.gloss: The boy is eating an apple.
The girl is eating an apple.
I’m buying the bread and the cheese.
My grandfather drinks tea and coffee.
The man is drinking a beer.
She is buying all kinds of fruit.
I’m buying the sugar and the salt.
The man is drinking the beer.
I drink neither tea nor coffee.
I have neither bread nor cheese.
You (to a woman) don’t like cheese.
The child neither eats nor drinks.
Is the boy eating an apple?
Do you (to a man) have sugar?
You (to a man) don’t like tea.

sentences.text: أَلَا تُحِبُّ الشَّايَ؟ بَلَى، أُحِبُّ الشَّايَ.
sentences.gloss: Don’t you like tea? — Oh yes, I do like tea.
Do you want tea or coffee?
Do you (to a woman) want water or juice?
Which do you like: fish or meat?
Do you (several) drink tea or coffee?
Would you like any sugar or milk?
Maybe my father will have tea.
Do you (to a woman) like fruit? — Of course!
Of course I want a coffee.
We’re buying bread and milk as well.

sentences.text: هَلْ تُرِيدُ شَايًا؟ نَعَمْ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
sentences.gloss: Would you like tea? — Yes, please.
Would you (to a woman) like coffee? — No, thank you.

sentences.text: هَلْ تُرِيدُ شَيْئًا؟ لَا شَيْءَ، شُكْرًا.
sentences.gloss: Do you want anything? — Nothing, thank you.
